decision: Atomic write via temp file in $HOME (.claude.json.luca-<pid>-<ts>.tmp) then rename over ~/.claude.json; mode tightened to 0600 but never loosened below an existing stricter mode
alternatives: plain writeFile over the primary config
temp file in os.tmpdir() then rename
reasoning: rename(2) is atomic only within the same filesystem, so the temp file must live in $HOME alongside the target (os.tmpdir may be a different volume). Plain writeFile risks truncation-on-crash of the user's PRIMARY config. Mode: file now holds a Bearer token so tighten to 0600, but a user with a stricter mode must not be loosened.
risk: If $HOME and the config target ever diverge onto different filesystems rename would EXDEV-fail; not a realistic case for ~/.claude.json.
reviewHint: Verify the temp-file lives in the SAME dir as ~/.claude.json so rename stays atomic.

decision: Three-case read guard (absent/ws->{}; parses->parsed; throws->abort) + inception-mode temp + unlink-on-failure
reasoning: Audit prescribed the exact three-case behavior; whitespace-only treated as safe first-run per spec. Inception mode via writeFile{mode} eliminates the 0644 token window; chmodSync kept for pre-existing inode
risk: Whitespace-only treated as empty could in theory mask a truncated config, but a 0-byte/ws file carries no recoverable data so {} is correct
